findings.message:
Unvalidated Markdown marker can bypass sanitization

`MARKDOWN_LINK_START_RE` matches any literal `](`, even without an opening link label. For `text ](Fixes #123)`, the destination scan protects `Fixes` and splits the keyword from its reference, so the directive is published unchanged. Only a valid Markdown link should create a protected range.

src/github/text.ts:85-89

Link titles are rewritten

`findMarkdownDestination` stops at the first whitespace and protects only the destination. A valid link such as `[link](/foo "Fixes #123")` therefore has its title rewritten to `" #123"`, despite link titles not being closing directives and the function promising byte preservation outside the keyword.

src/github/text.ts:43-47

Reference-definition labels are rewritten

The reference-definition match consumes the label, but the protected range starts only after `]:`. Thus `[Fixes #123]: /foo` becomes `[#123]: /foo`, changing a valid reference label and potentially breaking later references.

src/github/text.ts:93-97

URL scanning absorbs prose after a closing bracket

`findUrlEnd` does not treat `]` as a delimiter. In `[https://example.test]Fixes #123`, it protects through the adjacent `Fixes` text, so the real directive is left unchanged instead of becoming `[https://example.test]#123`. Structural closing punctuation needs to terminate the URL while preserving valid bracketed URL syntax.

src/github/text.ts:68-79

GitHub issue-URL closing form is never stripped

The closing-reference lookahead accepts only `#N` and `owner/repo#N`. Because URL ranges are copied verbatim, `Fixes: https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123` remains in the published body even though this repository treats GitHub issue URLs as issue-closing references. The URL form must be recognized before protecting URL ranges.

src/github/text.ts:17-18

summary: The sanitizer still has several Markdown and URL parsing gaps that either rewrite non-directive content or allow closing directives to survive.
